scope: Proposition 5.1 (Effective divisor arithmetic) of the manuscript “Deterministic Polynomial Factorization over Prime Fields” (preprints/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields-October-4-2026/Deterministic-Polynomial-Factorization-over-Prime-Fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 142 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ed88aa5ba802311a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On the curve C above, the following operations are deterministic and use a number of field operations polynomial in q, N, the degrees occurring in the input representation, the absolute degrees of the divisors materialized during the operation, and the parameter ℓ in the third operation: 1. divisor addition, negation, coefficientwise minimum and maximum, and the action of σ; 2. construction of the divisor of an explicitly represented nonzero function, and evaluation of its valuation and leading coefficient at a specified ramification point or point at infinity; 3. computation of the Riemann–Roch space L(D + ℓ∞0) for ℓ ≥ 0; 4. replacement of a degree-zero divisor D by a linearly equivalent divisor D′ satisfying ∥D′∥ ≤ 2g, with a function a such that D′ = D + div(a). These algorithms do not require factorization of the polynomials defining the finite sup- ports. Their decisions use only field zero tests, so they admit simultaneous execution as in Lemma 2.1.
